tools.name: list_psr_types
tools.description:
List production-type (psr_type) codes. Pass zone= to scope the answer.

Most codes are ENTSO-E's B01..B25 and mean the same thing in every
ENTSO-E zone. A few are source-native (source != "entsoe") and exist only
where that source publishes — they express concepts the B-codes cannot,
so they are NOT interchangeable with a similar-looking B-code. Check
`source` and read `description` before comparing a code across zones.

Passing zone= also returns `taxonomy_note` for zones that mix taxonomies
(e.g. GB), and per-code `endpoints` showing where each code comes from.

Each code carries `counts_as_generation`: when False the figure is a net
flow or net storage number, not production — do not sum it into a
generation total.

tools.name: get_series
tools.description:
Generic time-series query for ANY registered series endpoint.

One tool covers every dataset except outages (call `list_endpoints()`
to see them all), so a new dataset needs no new tool to learn.

Argument shape adapts to the endpoint:
  • single-zone (day_ahead_price, actual_load, generation_per_type, …)
    → pass `zone="DE_LU"`
  • cross-zone  (crossborder_flow, scheduled_exchanges,
                 net_transfer_capacity_dayahead)
    → pass `from_zone="DE_LU"` AND `to_zone="FR"`
  • psr-dependent (generation_per_type, wind_solar_forecast,
                   installed_generation_capacity)
    → optionally filter via `psr_types=["solar","wind_onshore"]`

`start`/`end`: UTC by default; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE
(for "all of April 2026" use end=2026-05-01). Pass `tz="local"` or an
IANA name to interpret as wall-clock in that timezone.

`aggregation`: 'raw' (default — native PT15M/PT60M per endpoint),
'hourly' (AVG over quarters → one row per hour, useful for the
growing list of PT15M-stored endpoints like DE_LU day_ahead_price),
'daily', or 'monthly'. For day-ahead prices specifically the auction
still clears hourly even where stored at PT15M, so AVG=any-quarter;
SUM would 4× over-count.

Currency: price columns keep `_eur_` in their names for stability. An
endpoint whose rows carry a `currency` column (day-ahead and intraday
prices, the A81/A15 capacity prices, activated_balancing_price,
imbalance_prices) labels each row (PLN, HUF, RON, CZK, GBP, …) and the
response `unit` follows it; `unit` is null when the window mixes
currencies (`mixed_currency`) or, for activated_balancing_price and
imbalance_prices, holds rows of unknown currency
(`currency_unknown_rows`). Never average a price across rows with
different `currency`.

Split periods: when a response carries `split_periods`, some periods hold
more than one row — different published series told apart by the listed
columns (activated_balancing_price: `product`, e.g. CZ/SK mFRR standard
A01 vs specific A02; or `currency`). Never average across them. Keep one
with `filters={"product": ["A01"]}` — `filters` takes any categorical
column of the endpoint (`{column: [values]}`).

Process types: activated balancing prices are one endpoint per ENTSO-E
processType (activated_balancing_price = A16 realised; _mfrr_scheduled =
A60, _mfrr_direct = A61, _afrr_local = A68) — different prices for the
same period, never to be merged. `related_series` names the siblings
holding data for the zone.

Ended series: a window reaching past the day a series stopped upstream
(a zone that left ENTSO-E, a frozen archive, a series that ended) carries
`series_ended` — the last day, why, and `successors`: the endpoints that
carry it on, each with a ready `call` and a `note` on how it differs. GB
day-ahead after 2020-12-31 → day_ahead_price_imrp (GBP/MWh); GB
generation after 2021-06-15 → generation_per_type_elexon (Elexon, the same
ENTSO-E codes) and generation_mix (NESO, with its estimate of embedded
wind).

Freshness: every answer carries `freshness` — the newest value stored
for the series (`newest`, UTC; the whole series, not only the window),
how far back its values are fetched again, at least weekly
(`rechecked_days`; 0 = not at all), the last day of a series its
publisher stopped (`stopped_after`) and, where the publisher's revision
lag is known, the date from which values may still change
(`revisable_from`, with `revision_basis` "measured" or "estimated"), with
a plain `note`. compare_zones, get_derivation and get_tb_spread carry it
too, one entry per series read.

Outage-family endpoints (different schema) stay on `get_outages()`.

tools.name: get_day_ahead_prices
tools.description:
Day-ahead clearing price for a bidding zone, in the zone's trading
currency (EUR for euro zones; the per-row `currency` column and the
response `unit` say which — GB=GBP, PL/RO/BG carry local-currency eras).

`start`/`end` default to UTC; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE.
For 'all of April 2026' use start=2026-04-01, end=2026-05-01
(end=2026-04-30 silently drops the final UTC day — and 1–2 local-time
hours of April for European zones in CET/CEST). The response's
`period` block shows the resolved window so you can verify
(a 30-day month is 720 hours).

`tz`: pass "local" to interpret start/end as wall-clock in the zone's
timezone, or an explicit IANA name like "Europe/Berlin". The server
converts to UTC at the boundary.

GB/UK: ENTSO-E's GB day-ahead price ended 2020-12-31, when GB left
European market coupling. For later windows use
`get_series(endpoint="day_ahead_price_imrp", zone="GB", …)` — the same
GB day-ahead auction, GBP/MWh, published ~D-2; a window past a series'
end answers with `series_ended`, naming the endpoint that carries it on.

If you're computing a **generation-weighted** price metric — capture
price, capture rate, value factor, merchant-PPA achieved price — use
`get_derivation(slug="capture_price", …)` instead. It runs server-side
over the full window and returns monthly rows; no row cap, no pagination.

tools.name: get_tb_spread
tools.description:
Top-Bottom (TBx) spread — daily battery-arbitrage benchmark.
TBx = sum(top X priced hours) − sum(bottom X priced hours) over the
day-ahead clearing prices for `zone` on `date`. The day is the SDAC
market day (23/25 hours on DST-transition days). `date` must be a
bare YYYY-MM-DD — time-bearing strings are rejected.
Returns both `spread` (<currency>/MW/day) and `mean_spread`
(<currency>/MWh = spread/X) in the zone's trading currency — see the
response `currency`/`unit` (EUR for euro zones; GB=GBP).
Common X: 1, 2, 4. A day past the zone's day-ahead series end (GB after
2020-12-31) answers with `series_ended`, naming the endpoint that carries
the prices on.

tools.name: get_load
tools.description:
Actual or forecast load (MW). kind = actual | forecast | both.

`start`/`end` default to UTC; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE.
For a full calendar month set `end` to the first day of the next
month. Pass `tz="local"` or an IANA name to interpret start/end as
wall-clock in that timezone.

GB/UK: ENTSO-E's GB load ended 2021-06-15. A later window answers with
`series_ended` naming `demand_outturn_transmission` (Elexon) — national
demand at the transmission boundary, ~5.5 GW below total load, not the
same quantity.

tools.name: get_generation
tools.description:
Aggregated generation (MW) per production type.

`start`/`end` default to UTC; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE.
For a full calendar month set `end` to the first day of the next
month. Pass `tz="local"` or an IANA name to interpret start/end as
wall-clock in that timezone.

GB/UK: ENTSO-E's GB generation ended 2021-06-15. For later windows in the
same ENTSO-E codes use `get_series(endpoint="generation_per_type_elexon",
zone="GB", …)` (Elexon, from 2021); for NESO's mix with its estimate of
embedded wind use `get_series(endpoint="generation_mix", zone="GB", …)`
(2009→now, its own wind codes — `list_psr_types(zone="GB")` first). A
window past a series' end answers with `series_ended`, naming both.

If you're computing a **generation-weighted** price metric — capture
price, capture rate, value factor, merchant-PPA achieved price — use
`get_derivation(slug="capture_price", …)` instead. It runs server-side
over the full window and returns monthly rows; no row cap, no pagination.

tools.name: get_crossborder_flow
tools.description:
Cross-border physical flow (MW) between two adjacent zones.

`start`/`end` default to UTC; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE.
`tz="local"` uses the FROM-zone's timezone; or pass an IANA name.

tools.name: get_outages
tools.description:
Generation-unit unavailability events (UMM).

`start`/`end` default to UTC; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE. An
outage is returned if it overlaps the window. Pass `tz="local"` or an
IANA name to interpret start/end as wall-clock in that timezone.
Each row is one unit's availability step, from its document's latest
revision. ENTSO-E lists some outages under several documents with
identical rows; each such row is served once, and `copies` counts the
documents that filed it. A unit can still have several overlapping
rows that differ. To total unavailable MW, count each unit once per
instant (its largest unavailable MW), not the sum of its rows.
A zone whose outage feed stopped upstream (GB, 2021-06-15) carries
`series_ended`: outages announced since then are missing, though older
documents may still schedule events into the window.

tools.name: compare_zones
tools.description:
Compare one endpoint across multiple zones.

`start`/`end` default to UTC; `start` inclusive, `end` EXCLUSIVE.
`tz="local"` is rejected (zones may differ); pass an explicit IANA
tz like "Europe/Berlin" if you need wall-clock alignment.
`filters={column: [values]}` keeps only rows whose categorical column
holds one of the values, in every zone (see get_series); zones whose
periods hold several rows are listed under `split_periods_by_zone`.
A zone whose series stopped upstream before the window's end (GB
day-ahead after 2020-12-31) is listed under `series_ended_by_zone`, with
the endpoint that carries it on — an empty `[]` there is not "no data
yet".

tools.name: data_coverage
tools.description:
Show what data is available and how current it is for (endpoint × zone)
— call before querying if you're not sure a recent date is available yet.
Each pair's newest year carries `latest_data_at`, its newest stored
record; `lag` grades every pair on how old that record is.

tools.name: list_derivations
tools.description:
List computed-metric derivations available via get_derivation().

Each derivation is a metric computed on the fly from one or more
stored datasets. Today: capture_price (monthly
VWAP capture price + baseload + capture rate per technology;
"capture rate" is the industry-standard name for what the JSON
response calls `quality_factor`), negative_price_hours, residual_load,
res_share, emissions (monthly CO2 emissions per fuel using IPCC
AR5 lifecycle factors, production-based), and tb_spread (monthly or
annual Top-Bottom battery-arbitrage spread TB1/TB2/TB4/TB6 per zone
on SDAC market days; accepts zone='all' for every zone in one call).

tools.name: get_derivation
tools.description:
Compute **capture price**, **capture rate** (a.k.a. value factor /
quality factor / Marktwertfaktor), **TBx battery-arbitrage spreads**,
and other generation-weighted market metrics server-side from the
stored data. Use this instead of fetching hourly prices + hourly generation
yourself and weighting them client-side — server-side aggregation has
no row cap and no pagination.

`slug`: a key from list_derivations() — today: `"capture_price"`,
`"negative_price_hours"`, `"residual_load"`, `"res_share"`,
`"emissions"`, `"tb_spread"`.

`tb_spread` returns monthly (default) or annual (aggregation='annual')
Top-Bottom spreads TB1/TB2/TB4/TB6 in <currency>/MW per period — the sum
of daily (top-x minus bottom-x hourly prices) over SDAC market days. The
only slug accepting `aggregation`, and the only one accepting
multi-zone `zone` ('all', a list, or CSV). Example — annual TB2 across
every European market in ONE call:
  get_derivation("tb_spread", "2025-01-01", "2026-01-01",
                 zone="all", aggregation="annual")
For a single day's top/bottom hour TIMESTAMPS use get_tb_spread.

`capture_price` returns monthly rows per (zone, psr_type, currency) with
columns: currency, capture_price_eur_per_mwh, baseload_price_eur_per_mwh,
quality_factor (the capture rate = capture/baseload), total_gen_mwh,
n_hours. Months are bucketed by local time using the zone's IANA
timezone.

ENDED INPUTS: when an input series stopped upstream before the window's
end, the answer carries `series_ended` (per zone for a multi-zone
tb_spread): which inputs, why, what carries each on, and any metric that
carries this one on. GB: ENTSO-E's day-ahead price ended 2020-12-31, so
GB capture_price, negative_price_hours and tb_spread stop there;
`capture_price_mid` covers GB 2016-09 → now against the Market Index
Price (a traded index, not the auction — read its note).

CURRENCY (capture_price and tb_spread alike): the `*_eur_per_mwh` /
`tb*_eur_per_mw` key names are FIXED for API stability and do NOT track
the actual unit — read the row's `currency` column, which is
authoritative (EUR for euro zones, GBP for GB, PLN/RON/BGN for the
PL/RO/BG local-currency eras). The response echoes it top-level as
`currency`; a window spanning two currencies instead sets `unit` to null
with `mixed_currency: true` and a `currencies` list. A month (or period)
spanning a redenomination splits into one row PER CURRENCY, each computed
only from that currency's hours — so never average or sum a price column
across rows with different `currency` values. Summing `total_gen_mwh`
across them IS correct: the split rows partition the month's hours rather
than duplicating them. `quality_factor` is a ratio and stays comparable
across currencies.

`emissions` returns monthly rows per (zone, psr_type) with columns:
generation_mwh, n_hours, emission_factor_kg_per_mwh, emissions_t_co2.
Production-based; IPCC AR5 lifecycle factors. Zero-emission rows
(nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, marine) appear with
emissions_t_co2 = 0 — useful for stacked charts.

Filter via `psr_types=["solar","wind_onshore","wind_offshore"]` (or
raw B-codes like "B16") to get only the technologies you care about.
Defaults to all psr_types that have generation data.

Example — Spain solar capture price, last 12 months:
  get_derivation("capture_price", "2025-05-01", "2026-05-01",
                 zone="ES", psr_types=["B16"], tz="Europe/Madrid")
Example — Germany 2024 emissions by fuel:
  get_derivation("emissions", "2024-01-01", "2025-01-01",
                 zone="DE_LU", tz="Europe/Berlin")
Returns 12 monthly rows in one call; no pagination.
